assessments.reasoning: The second paragraph of the pinned project notice expressly names COPYING.LGPL as the base. The closing contact paragraph repeats the filename. Neither passage assigns a version number.

Both parts identify root COPYING.LGPL.txt at b51eb6f0e87da578205ddcc993fe0674a8766178, with whole-file SHA-256 7a4436f9ec37603356791c87de3bc444989befd2682d29efb3d97604e04c1852. The contiguous ranges [0,16384) and [16384,25275) cover the heading through the application example.
The pinned SPDX detail identifies the relevant paragraph and archive. It gives no base filename or edition. The 2.0 in its exception identifier cannot establish the base version.

challenge.method: Compared the named sibling with Free Pascal’s rtl/COPYING.txt and checked whether the application example at the end of the Lazarus base establishes a version election for every unit.
challenge.results: The Free Pascal sibling says Lesser version 2.1, February 1999, which would give the wrong answer for Lazarus. Lazarus’s section 13 discusses version choices, and its closing “How to Apply” example offers later versions. That example is guidance for authors. The Lazarus notice itself directs the reader to unit headers.

limitations: The edition finding applies to the accompanying document. An only-version or later-version election for a particular unit requires its applicable notice.
reasoning: The Lazarus notice says “see the file COPYING.LGPL”. At the same Lazarus commit the accompanying root file is COPYING.LGPL.txt. Its heading reads “GNU LIBRARY GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE”, “Version 2, June 1991”. LGPL-2.0 accurately describes the edition carried with this notice.
